verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. (1) Nothing is missing. The heading is transcribed verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42525 as '## D.3.5.3 Subscripting example', preceded by the correct anchor '' (line 42524). The kind label 'missing-heading' misdescribes its own evidence -- the claim's pdf_says and markdown_says quote the SAME heading text, differing only in the count of '#' characters. No prose on page 1061 is lost either: the PDF's opening continuation paragraph ('associated; however, the manner of correspondence is determined by the implementor...') is present, correctly reflowed into the tail of the page-1060 block. (2) The claimed PDF fact is not a PDF fact. I rendered both pages at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs. On page 1060 the PDF sets 'D.3.5 Subscripting', 'D.3.5.1 General' and 'D.3.5.2 Subscripting using index-names' in the SAME bold face at the SAME point size with the SAME left margin -- the parent D.3.5 and its children D.3.5.1/D.3.5.2 are typographically indistinguishable. Page 1061 sets 'D.3.5.3 Subscripting example' identically. The PDF therefore encodes clause depth SOLELY in the dotted clause number, and the markdown reproduces that number exactly. The information the claim says is lost was never carried by typography in the source, and it is fully carried by 'D.3.5.3' in the transcription. (3) Markdown heading level here is formatting, not content, and it is a systemic property of the transcription rather than a page-1061 defect. The pipeline assigns heading levels page-locally: the first clause heading after each '## Page NNNN' marker is emitted at '##' and later headings on the same page nest below it. The same reset appears throughout Annex D at exactly the page seams -- '#### D.2.2.1' followed by '## D.2.2.2', '#### D.2.3.2.2' followed by '## D.2.3.2.3', '### D.2.3.3.2' followed by '## D.2.3.3.3', '#### D.6.1.1' followed by '## D.6.1.2'. Document-wide, 4-component annex clause numbers are emitted 26 times at '##' versus 23 times at '###'; 3-component numbers 79 times at '##' versus 48 at '###'. Flagging one instance of a global convention as a per-page structural discrepancy would generate hundreds of identical findings and identify no lost spec content. Nothing about COBOL semantics, syntax, or the citability of D.3.5.3 changes.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading 'D.3.5.3 Subscripting example' is present verbatim in the markdown with a correct 'section-d-3-5-3' anchor, and no page-1061 prose is missing. The PDF prints D.3.5, D.3.5.1, D.3.5.2 and D.3.5.3 in identical bold type at identical size and margin, so printed depth is conveyed only by the dotted clause number -- which the transcription preserves exactly. The '##' vs '###' difference is a formatting artifact of page-local heading-level assignment that recurs at page seams throughout the transcription (e.g. D.2.2.2, D.2.3.2.3, D.2.3.3.3, D.6.1.2), not a content loss on this page.
